# Voice and Tone

This is the compiled voice, tone, and style hub for Simpro brand writing. Use it before drafting blogs, PPC, landing pages, sales copy, and AI-agent prompts.

## Voice Principles

Simpro voice should be practical, direct, trade-aware, confident, clear, and outcome-oriented. The writing should sound like it understands operational pressure in field service without exaggerating claims or leaning on vague software jargon.

## Writing Rules

- Write in plain business language with field-service context.
- Tie features to operational or commercial outcomes when source support exists.
- Avoid inflated AI language, generic productivity claims, or unsupported ROI promises.
- Keep exact customer quotes, metrics, and review claims source-gated.
- Localize spelling, examples, regulatory references, and terminology without changing core positioning.

## Named-Author Blog Voice

- Named-author Simpro blogs and thought leadership may use first-person judgment, contractions, operational scenes, decisive opinions, and short punchlines.
- Author opinion must remain distinguishable from empirical fact.
- Metrics, market comparisons, product status, roadmap statements, and commercial claims remain proof gated.
- Em dashes are prohibited. Use a period, comma, colon, or parentheses when the grammar supports it.
- Product pages and landing pages retain their existing restrained channel treatment.

Overview: Purpose & How This Doc Will Be Used (Read First) {#overview:-purpose-&-how-this-doc-will-be-used-(read-first)}
This Core Messaging Repository is the single source of strategic truth used to power AI-assisted content creation at scale.
It defines the global messaging constitution for Simpro and establishes the universal strategic truth that all downstream messaging inherits from.
This repository consolidates Simpro’s internal positioning — including category definition, message house, value pillars, economic framing, work environment logic, business maturity and technology posture, role-based value emphasis, target customer boundaries, AI positioning principles, and tone standards.
These internal strategic constructs define how Simpro competes and communicates. This document operationalizes them into a unified messaging system that governs how all external messaging is created.
External campaigns, vertical assets, collateral, and AI-generated content are downstream expressions of this internal positioning — not independent strategy. This document ensures that external messaging remains anchored to internal strategic truth.
All outward-facing communication must inherit from the internal structure defined here.
It governs how all Simpro messaging aligns to:

Strategic positioning
Value pillars
Profitability outcome framing
Work environments (residential, commercial and hybrid)
Work types (installation, inspection, testing, maintenance, and repair)
Work complexity (small jobs, recurring contracts, and mid-sized projects)
Role-based value emphasis (leadership, operations, office staff, finance, field teams)
Customer archetypes (business maturity and technology posture)
Target customer boundaries
AI positioning principles (product-level)
Tone & voice standards
Guardrails and positioning constraints
Integration of new go-to-market launches

It is designed as a long-lived strategic foundation — not a campaign document or short-term messaging brief.
This document is not campaign copy, a brochure, or a sales deck.
It is the strategic messaging operating system derived from Simpro’s internal positioning, powering all downstream content and governing how messaging is created.

What This Document Enables
This repository serves as the strategic foundation for:

Vertical brief development
Structured integration of new functionality through GTM Extension Intake Framework (Section 11)
Product Marketing launch and capability positioning
Consistency and alignment in campaign and sales enablement
AI-powered content generation and prompt governance

All Simpro messaging must ladder back to this foundation.
This document governs Simpro messaging specifically. Other brands within the portfolio may develop parallel Core Messaging Repositories aligned to their own positioning.

How the System Is Used in Practice
It is not the day-to-day drafting tool.

—-----------------------

—---------------------
Who Uses What:
1.  Product Marketing Managers:  Operate at the strategic and integration layer. They:

Complete the structured GTM Extension Intake Form (explained in section 11 of this Core Messaging Repository and housed in the GTM Extension Intake Library) as part of the official go-to-market process for new capabilities, add-ons, or platform modules.

Structured positioning outputs
First-pass launch messaging
First-pass content for campaigns, collateral, landing pages, etc

Reference the Core Messaging Repository when evolving positioning or making structural messaging decisions.
Ensure new functionality reinforces — and does not alter — Core Messaging.

2.  Writers (across Marketing & Enablement):  Operate at the execution layer. They:

Core Messaging Repository
Vertical Profile Library (when vertical content is required)
GTM Extension Intake Library (when capability messaging is required)

Do not redefine positioning or modify Core Messaging

—-----------------------------
Governance Principle:
AI applies positioning defined here — it does not invent it.
All AI-generated output must:

Reflect unified value pillars
Anchor in profitability and trade business economics
Apply work environment logic
Apply business maturity and role nuance
Operate within defined tone and guardrails

When This Document Is Updated
This repository is updated only when structural positioning changes occur, including:

Major updates to the Simpro Message Map, including introduction of new value pillars or strategic positioning shifts
Formal updates to Brand or Tone & Voice standards
Material shift in AI philosophy
Change in target market scope
Structural change to work environment logic
Structural change to Business Maturity and technology posture (Customer Archetype) model
Structural changes to buyer or user role taxonomy

New capabilities, add-ons, modules, or collateral do not modify this document; they integrate through the Simpro GTM Intake Framework (Section 11), documented within the GTM Extension Intake Library, as governed supplements.
Core Messaging is version-controlled and updated deliberately and rarely — not reactively.

Anchor Positioning {#anchor-positioning}

1.1 Category Definition
Simpro is:

The AI-first operating platform for trade and field service businesses.
Simpro is not:

An ERP
A general contractor project management system
Industrial asset management software
Infrastructure construction software
A replacement for accounting systems

These boundaries are non-negotiable positioning constraints
Authoring Guidance:

Use “operating platform” as the primary category description.
Avoid positioning Simpro as ERP or generic “software.”

1.2 Mission Framing (Constitutional)
Simpro exists to:

Change the economics of trade businesses.
Replace operational chaos with clarity and control.
Protect and expand profitability through real-time operational visibility.

Profitability is framed as economic control, expressed through:

Margin protection and expansion
Revenue growth through operational clarity
Cost visibility
Cash flow acceleration
Scalable growth without administrative expansion

Authoring Guidance:

Do not promise fixed outcomes (e.g., “double profitability”).
Tie profitability to operational discipline and visibility.
Avoid hyperbolic or absolute claims.

1.3 Economic Philosophy
Core belief → Profit is clarity.
When trade businesses see labor costs, materials, WIP, and cash position in real time, better decisions follow. Clarity precedes control. Control enables profitability.
Operational complexity and fragmentation are not inevitable; Chaos is solvable through connected systems.
Authoring Guidance:

Elevate operational clarity as the driver of financial confidence.
Avoid productivity claims without financial linkage.

Core Value Pillars {#core-value-pillars}
These pillars operationalize the Simpro Message House into authoring-ready constructs
They are structurally fixed across verticals and work environments.

They are emphasis-modulated, not rewritten.
All pillar authoring assumes mandatory profitability linkage and outcome-first framing.

Pillar 1 — Confidence in Profitability

Definition

Real-time visibility into job-level costs, margins, labor efficiency, and financial performance before a job is completed.

Key Outcomes

Margin protection
Early risk detection
Reduced cost overruns
Stronger forecasting confidence
Authoring Guidance

Emphasize in-progress visibility over after-the-fact reporting.
Tie workflow improvements to financial impact.

Avoid generic “improved efficiency” without economic framing.

Pillar 2 — Operational Visibility and Control from Quote to Cash

Definition:

End-to-end visibility and control across the full lifecycle - establishing visibility and control from quote through cash.

Initial Contact → Estimate → Schedule → Dispatch → Job Execution → Inventory → Assets → Compliance Documentation → Mobile Field Workflows → Invoice → Payment → Reporting and Insights → Ongoing Customer Communications
Actual lifecycle order may vary by company or work

Key Outcomes

Reduced lifecycle friction
Faster quote turnaround
Shorter payment cycles
Unified reporting
Improved cross-team operational control
Authoring Guidance

Use lifecycle framing:
Emphasize both visibility and control across the full lifecycle, not isolated task coordination.
Avoid disconnected feature lists.

Reinforce decision-making authority enabled by control.

Pillar 3 — Smarter Field-to-Office Workflows

Definition

Connected workflows that eliminate duplication, reduce manual rework, and align field execution with office control – ensuring real-time executional coordination between field and office.

Key Outcomes

Reduced administrative load
Increased technician utilization through smarter scheduling and dispatch coordination
Improved technician productivity
Better communication
Fewer errors and callbacks
Improved technician retention through reduced operational friction
Authoring Guidance

Emphasize friction removal and coordination.
Avoid abstract “streamlined” claims without mechanism.

Focus on handoff, synchronization, and execution continuity between people and systems

Pillar 4 — AI-Powered Automation (Enabler)

Pillar 4 functions as an enabler of the first 3 pillars, not an independent outcome category.

Definition

Embedded intelligence that removes repetitive admin, surfaces risk early, and strengthens financial outcomes.

AI Philosophy

AI augments skilled professionals.
It does not replace them.

Authoring Guidance

Frame AI as operational leverage.
Avoid replacement narratives or future roadmap claims.

Profitability & Work Environment Framework {#profitability-&-work-environment-framework}

3.1 Core Economic Model
Simpro’s messaging is grounded in a unified economic progression:
Operational Friction → Revenue Leakage → Margin Erosion → Cash Flow Delay → Strategic Constraint → Scalable Growth
This progression defines Simpro’s core economic logic and applies across all verticals, work environments, and business maturity levels.
Authoring Guidance:

Escalate workflow improvements to clear economic impact (i.e. margin, revenue, cash flow or strategic capacity).
Do not stop at “efficiency” language.

3.2 Profitability Drivers
Profitability within trade businesses is influenced by:

Accurate estimating
Labor utilization
Materials cost control
Scheduling efficiency
Change order visibility
Speed to invoice
Payment collection speed
Reduced rework and callbacks
Compliance accuracy

Authoring Guidance:

Connect operational improvements to at least one profitability driver.
Avoid abstract “improvement” claims.

3.3 Work Environment — Common Challenges and Financial Pressures
The economic model itself does not change by work environment.
However, common challenges and financial pressures differ depending on the environment:

Residential

Lower revenue per job increases dependence on volume efficiency.
Short job duration increases scheduling and dispatch sensitivity.
Field payment collection is critical to maintaining cash flow.
High job frequency increases risk of admin overload and callbacks.
Commercial

Larger contract values increase exposure to cost overruns.
Limited visibility into work-in-progress increases forecasting risk.
Phased or multi-stage jobs extend revenue recognition timelines.
Approval workflows, invoicing terms, and accounts payable cycles delay cash realization.
Compliance and documentation requirements increase financial exposure.
Change order mismanagement impacts profitability.
Hybrid

Mixed job structures create coordination and forecasting complexity.
Balancing high-volume work with contract discipline creates operational friction.
Resource allocation across job types impacts revenue predictability.

3.4 Work Environment — Value Emphasis
Work environment affects value emphasis — not core pillars or economic model.
Messaging should shift based on where financial pressure originates.

Residential Value Emphasis

Emphasize speed, scheduling accuracy, and dispatch efficiency.
Highlight field payment collection and invoice speed.
Reinforce reduced callbacks and return visits.
Focus on volume efficiency and daily operational clarity.
Primary pillar emphasis often skews toward:
Operational visibility and control
Field-to-office workflow efficiency

Commercial Value Emphasis

Emphasize margin protection and cost control.
Highlight work-in-progress visibility and forecasting accuracy.
Reinforce compliance documentation and change order discipline.
Focus on revenue predictability and financial control.
Primary pillar emphasis often skews toward:
Confidence in profitability
Operational visibility and control

Hybrid Value Emphasis

Lead with commercial-style margin and coordination control.
Reinforce residential-style speed and efficiency where relevant.
Emphasize unified systems managing mixed job structures.
Primary pillar emphasis balances:
Profitability control
Workflow coordination
Cash flow strength

Authoring Guidance:

Adjust emphasis and examples without restating the economic model.
Avoid implying sophistication hierarchy.
Always unify messaging to revenue, margin, and cash flow strength.

AI Capabilities: Positioning & Emphasis Scaling {#ai-capabilities:-positioning-&-emphasis-scaling}

4.1 Role of AI (Platform-Level Philosophy)
AI is positioned as an embedded operational advantage within the Simpro operating platform.
AI is an enabler of operational clarity and profitability — not a separate value system.
AI capabilities within Simpro exist to:

Reduce manual administrative work
Surface risk earlier
Improve data accuracy
Accelerate decision-making
Eliminate operational waste that erodes revenue and margin

AI is not positioned as:

A replacement for skilled tradespeople
A fully autonomous decision-maker
A guaranteed profit engine
A standalone product detached from operational workflows

Authoring Guidance:

Tie AI capabilities to real operational workflows and at least one profitability driver.
Avoid abstract “AI-powered” claims without any context.

4.2 Acceptable AI Claims
AI may be described as:

Automating repetitive administrative tasks
Highlighting trends or anomalies
Assisting with forecasting and profitability insights
Improving documentation accuracy
Reducing data entry burden
Enhancing dashboard and reports visibility

AI should not be described as:

Fully autonomous scheduling or dispatch
Replacing human judgment
Predicting exact revenue or margin outcomes
Making independent strategic decisions

4.3 AI Emphasis Based on Operational Complexity
AI emphasis should reflect operational complexity — not company size or perceived sophistication.
Greater complexity (higher volume, contract work, compliance demands, multi-team coordination) creates more opportunity for automation to remove waste and protect revenue and margin.
Less complex operations still benefit from AI, but messaging should remain practical and grounded in immediate workflow improvements.
Authoring Guidance:

Increase AI emphasis where workflow complexity increases.
Keep AI messaging practical and outcome-focused.
Avoid implying hierarchy between residential, commercial, or hybrid businesses.

4.4 AI Within Simpro (Capabilities or Add-Ons) or Platform (Modules or Products)
AI may be embedded within Simpro capabilities, add-ons, or platform modules (e.g., documentation tools, reporting capabilities, workflow automation features).
In those cases:

AI reinforces one or more core value pillars & remains grounded in operational workflow impact.
AI must not be positioned as independent from the broader Simpro operating platform.

The detailed mapping of AI-enabled add-ons or modules is governed by:

Section 11 — Simpro GTM Extension Intake Framework
Authoring Guidance:

Tie AI within a specific capability, add-on or module to the pillar it strengthens.
Do not present AI as a standalone product category unless formally packaged as such.

Customer Archetype Escalation Logic  {#customer-archetype-escalation-logic}
Simpro messaging adapts based on business maturity and technology posture of trade businesses we are targeting.
The three archetypes represent operational evolution — not company size or revenue level.
Archetypes reflect operational maturity and systems reliance — not business quality or intelligence.

5.1 Customer Archetype Definitions

Empower: Business seeking modernization away from manual/paper
Businesses transitioning from:

Paper-based processes
Manual coordination
Disconnected spreadsheets, calendars, and other basic tech tools
Limited operational visibility
Primary pressures:
Administrative overload
Lack of margin clarity
Inefficient scheduling
Inconsistent documentation
Primary value emphasis:
Replace manual processes
Simplify daily operations
Build operational clarity
Reduce administrative friction
Typical KPI focus:
Time saved on admin
Jobs per technician per day
Invoice turnaround time
Visibility into job margin
Authoring Guidance:
Use plain, practical language.
Emphasize ease of transition and immediate wins.

Avoid advanced analytics framing.

Elevate: Growth and scale-minded expander that is already using some software
Businesses experiencing growth strain:

Tool sprawl
Process inconsistency
Margin leakage
Limited cross-team visibility
Primary pressures:
Forecasting gaps
Revenue unpredictability
Increasing admin load
Primary value emphasis:
Standardize operations
Strengthen margin control
Improve cross-team coordination
Scale without proportional admin growth
Typical KPI focus:
Gross margin consistency
Revenue predictability
Labor utilization rate
Change order capture
Authoring Guidance:
Emphasize process consistency and financial control.
Introduce stronger reporting and visibility.

Tie improvements to predictable revenue growth.

Excel: Mature, data-driven optimizer
Businesses with established systems seeking advanced performance:

Multi-entity operations
Contract complexity
Advanced reporting needs
Strategic growth planning
Primary pressures:
Forecast precision
Cross-entity visibility
Data reliability
Strategic margin optimization
Primary value emphasis:
Advanced financial insight
Enterprise-level visibility
Data-driven decision-making
Optimization of revenue and margin performance
Typical KPI focus:
Forecast accuracy
Multi-entity margin comparison
Revenue per technician
Strategic growth rate
Authoring Guidance:
Lean into intelligence, analytics, and forecasting.
Avoid basic modernization language.
Emphasize strategic performance optimization.

5.2 Archetype Guardrails
Archetypes describe operational maturity — not intelligence, sophistication, or business quality.
Avoid implying that one archetype is “better” than another.

Messaging should escalate in sophistication — not superiority.

Role & Title Taxonomy {#role-&-title-taxonomy}
Simpro messaging must reflect the different priorities of decision-makers, influencers, and users.
Roles influence emphasis — not core value pillars.
Role-based modulation adjusts emphasis and language — not strategic positioning.

6.1 Role Categories

Executive Leadership: (i.e. Owner, CEO, Managing Director, General Manager)
Primary concerns:

Profitability and revenue growth
Strategic visibility and control
Cash flow strength
Long-term scalability and risk mitigation
Value emphasis:
Margin protection and expansion
Revenue predictability
Business-wide operational control and decision confidence
Authoring Guidance:
Lead with economic impact.
Tie operational improvements to business performance.

Avoid tactical feature detail unless tied to financial outcome.

Business Operations: (i.e. Operations manager, service manager, project manager)
Primary concerns:

Schedule efficiency
Labor utilization
Workflow consistency
Resource coordination
Job profitability
Value emphasis:
Operational visibility and control
Dispatch optimization
Standardized processes and reduced rework
Authoring Guidance:
Emphasize control and coordination.

Tie operational improvement to margin protection.

Office Staff: (i.e. Office manager, dispatcher, scheduler, administrator)
Primary concerns:

Administrative workload
Scheduling accuracy
Documentation management
Invoicing speed
Field communication
Value emphasis:
Reduced manual entry
Workflow clarity
Faster invoicing
Fewer errors
Authoring Guidance:
Emphasize simplicity and time savings.

Avoid strategic abstraction.

Finance Leadership:  (i.e. CFO, finance manager, controller, accounts receivable manager)
Primary concerns:

Cost control
Margin accuracy
Timely payments from customers
Cash flow management
Forecast reliability
Financial reporting integrity
Value emphasis:
Accurate job costing
Real-time financial visibility
Reduced revenue leakage
Improved invoice accuracy and collection speed
Authoring Guidance:
Use financial language.
Emphasize visibility, controls, and accuracy.

Avoid operational framing without financial linkage.

Field Technicians: (i.e. Technician, engineer, installer, field staff, crew)
Primary concerns:

Clear job instructions
Mobile access to information
Reduced paperwork
Accurate time and materials capture
Minimal disruption
Value emphasis:
Mobile access to job data
Simplified documentation
Faster job completion and fewer callbacks
Authoring Guidance:
Avoid surveillance or micromanagement framing.
Emphasize support, not control.

6.2 Role-Based Guardrails

Do not use identical messaging across all roles.
Economic impact may be framed differently depending on audience.
Always maintain alignment with core value pillars.
Do not introduce role-specific positioning shifts.

6.3 Role Simplification for Smaller Businesses
In smaller trade businesses, formal role separation may not exist.
In these cases, messaging should simplify to two primary audiences:
Owner / Leader

Responsible for revenue, margin, and overall business performance.
Office / Operations
Responsible for scheduling, coordination, invoicing, and daily execution.
Note: sometimes in smaller trade businesses, the “owner” is also one of a small number of skilled trades technicians that perform work in the field.
Authoring Guidance:
Combine financial and operational value where appropriate.
Avoid assuming enterprise-level departmental structure.
Maintain clarity and simplicity in role references.

Tone & Voice Standards {#tone-&-voice-standards}
This section translates the official Simpro Voice & Tone Guide into enforceable authoring standards within the Core Messaging framework.
It governs tone across AI-generated and human-written content without redefining brand positioning.
It applies to:

AI-generated content
Human-written content
Vertical briefs
Add-on and module messaging
Sales and marketing materials

Tone governs delivery.

Positioning governs substance.
Voice remains consistent across regions. Localization may adjust spelling, terminology, and phrasing – not brand personality.

7.1 Core Voice Attributes
Simpro’s voice is:

Confident and direct
Practical and trade-savvy
Human and outcome-oriented
Bold but evidence-backed
Clear and concise

Simpro’s voice is not:

Corporate or bureaucratic
Overly technical or buzzword-heavy
Overhyped or sensational
Patronizing
Casual to the point of unprofessional

7.2 Communication Principles
Messaging should:

Lead with pain or value and connect quickly to business impact.
Introduce technology after the economic or operational problem is clear.
Emphasize outcomes before features.
Use plain language.
Remain concise and structured.

Avoid:

Feature dumping
Dense paragraphs
Unexplained acronyms
Abstract transformation claims
Filler adjectives or buzzwords
“Best-in-class” style claims
Patronizing language

7.3 AI-Specific Tone Discipline
When referencing AI capabilities:

Keep AI language grounded and operational.
Tie AI to workflow improvement and financial outcomes.
Avoid sensational, replacing skilled professionals, or overhyped framing.

AI should feel:

Practical
Embedded
Useful
Credible

7.4 Role-Based Tone Adjustments
Tone may adjust slightly by audience:
Executive / Finance:

More economic and strategic language
Office / Operations:
More workflow and control-focused
Field:
More practical and task-oriented
Small businesses:
More straightforward and less formal

Core voice attributes remain constant across audiences.

7.5 “Simpro Test” for Messaging Quality
Before finalizing messaging, ensure:

Does it clearly connect to revenue, margin, or cash flow?
Is it operationally grounded?
Would a trade business leader respect it?
Is the customer positioned as the hero, not the product?
Is the language clear and concise?

If the answer is no to any of the above, revise.

Guardrails & Positioning Boundaries {#guardrails-&-positioning-boundaries}
This section defines non-negotiable positioning boundaries that protect strategic focus and market clarity.
Guardrails prevent positioning drift and ensure messaging remains aligned with Simpro’s market focus.

8.1 Market Scope Boundaries
Simpro supports and is positioned for:

Trade and field service businesses
Work completed in residential, commercial, and hybrid environments (installation, repair, inspection, testing, and maintenance work; small jobs, recurring contracts, mid-sized projects)

Simpro does not support, is not positioned for, and messaging must not imply:

Industrial work environments (e.g., heavy industrial facilities, refineries, manufacturing plants)
General contractor-led construction project management
Large-scale complex projects lasting more than one year (e.g., infrastructure or multi-year multi-site rollouts)

These boundaries are strategic market limits, not temporary capability gaps.

8.2 Category Boundaries
Simpro is not positioned as:

Industrial project management software
ERP (of any kind)
Engineering design management platforms
A replacement for accounting systems (e.g. QuickBooks or Xero)

Simpro integrates with accounting systems; it does not replace them.

8.3 Economic Claim Discipline
All economic claims must be grounded in:

Operational improvements
Verified customer testimonials and/or measurable proof metrics
Validated internal metrics
Credible third-party research or verified industry data

Avoid:

Unverified statistics or unsupported performance claims
Unattributed industry averages
Exaggerated ROI claims

Guardrails are non-negotiable and enforced through:

Core Messaging
GTM Extension Intake Framework review

Hero Messaging Usage {#hero-messaging-usage}
Hero messaging is a brand-level narrative device used to elevate positioning.
It must be used sparingly and is not a structural messaging layer or a vertical-level concept.

9.1 Purpose of Hero Framing
Hero messaging may be used to:

Frame a bold outcome-driven introduction
Anchor strategic positioning at the beginning of key assets
Reinforce confidence in profitability
Support high-impact calls-to-action

Hero messaging should not focus on features; it should focus on:

Outcome
Control
Confidence
Profitability

Hero framing does not override pillar discipline or profitability linkage

9.2 Where Hero Messaging May Be Used (Sparingly)
Hero framing may be used sparingly in:

Collateral headers and introductions
Landing page headlines
Executive-level messaging
Select thought leadership and campaign assets

It should not be:

Repeated across sections
Used in every asset
Embedded inside vertical briefs as structural logic

Localization Standards (NA; UK; ANZ) {#localization-standards-(na;-uk;-anz)}
Localization adjusts language and terminology — not positioning, pillars, economic framing, or voice.
Core Messaging remains structurally consistent across regions.
Localization may adjust terminology and phrasing for clarity, but not brand personality or voice.

10.1 What Localization May Adjust
Localization may adapt:

Spelling
Terminology (role titles, estimating language, vehicle terms)
Regulatory references and compliance norms
Regionally relevant work environment examples
Currency
Date formats
Regional customer testimonials and proof metrics
Local partner logos and ecosystem references
References to region-specific accounting or compliance norms

Localization may slightly adjust phrasing for cultural clarity, but must maintain:

Core voice attributes
Pillar alignment
Profitability framing
AI positioning principles
Guardrails

10.2 What Localization Must Not Change
Localization must not:

Rewrite value pillars
Change the economic framework
Introduce new positioning
Soften or exaggerate AI claims
Create region-specific versions of Simpro’s identity
Create region-specific positioning narratives
Expand or contract market scope

Simpro remains:

An AI-powered operating platform
Focused on residential and commercial trade businesses
Anchored in revenue, margin, and cash flow

10.3 Baseline Terminology & Spelling Reference
The following reflects localization patterns in current Simpro regional collateral (datasheets & brochures) and establishes baseline governance; It may be expanded as formal localization standards evolve.

Spelling Conventions

North America: labor; organization; program; optimize; color
UK / Australia / New Zealand:  labour; organisation; programme; optimise; colour
Terminology
Reflect common regional trade language without altering meaning:

North America: technician; dispatcher; field staff; truck; estimate
UK: engineer; scheduler; field engineer; van; quote
Australia / New Zealand: technician; scheduler; field technician; vehicle; quote
Financial & Compliance References

Currency must reflect region (USD, GBP, AUD, NZD).
Regulatory references must reflect regional standards.
Payment terms may vary by region.
Customer Proof & Ecosystem
Localization should include:
Regionally relevant customer testimonials and/or proof metrics
Regionally relevant partner logos and ecosystem references
Links to regional success stories where available

---
10.4 Authoring Guidance

Adjust terminology, not positioning.
Preserve economic clarity and global pillars alignment.
Do not introduce regional improvisation of strategy.
Ensure regional proof reinforces profitability framing.

GTM Extension Intake Framework (Capabilities; Add-ons; Modules) {#gtm-extension-intake-framework-(capabilities;-add-ons;-modules)}
This section defines the governing framework for how Simpro capabilities, add-ons, and platform modules integrate into Core Messaging.
The operational documentation of this framework is maintained in the separate GTM Extension Intake Library, which houses structured Intake Forms for individual capabilities, add-ons, and modules.
The Core Messaging Repository defines the integration rules.

The GTM Extension Intake Library documents how each extension reinforces those rules.
Extensions strengthen the system — they do not expand or restructure it.

11.1 Purpose
The Simpro GTM Extension Intake Framework ensures:

All capability messaging aligns with core value pillars
Add-ons and modules strengthen value and profitability positioning
Packaging decisions do not alter strategic messaging
Product expansion does not fragment positioning

This framework applies to:

Included Simpro capabilities
Paid Simpro add-ons
Paid platform modules
Cross-sell offerings

This framework documents both existing and future Simpro capabilities, add-ons, and platform modules within the Core Messaging structure.

11.2 Structural Principle
Core Messaging defines:

Economic model
Value pillars
Work environment logic
Business maturity and technology posture logic
Role-based value emphasis
AI positioning
Tone and guardrails

GTM Extensions define:

How specific functionality reinforces that structure.

No GTM Extension may:

Introduce a new value pillar
Override profitability framing
Change work environment positioning
Alter archetype logic
Alter AI philosophy

11.3 Extension Integration Model

Every Simpro capability, add-on, and platform module - new or existing - must reinforce the Core Messaging structure.
At minimum, every GTM Extension must:

Reinforce one or more core value pillars
Link to at least one profitability driver
Align with work environment logic
Reflect business maturity and technology posture nuance
Reflect role-based value emphasis

They integrate into the existing framework by clarifying how specific capabilities strengthen profitability, operational control, and scalability.
Operational details for documenting this integration are defined in Section 11.5 (Required PMM Inputs).

11.4 Required PMM Inputs – GTM Intake Form (in collaboration with Product Mgt)
Completion of the GTM Extension Intake Form is required as part of the official go-to-market process for GTMs involving new capabilities, add-ons, or platform modules.
This Intake Form serves as a governed supplement to Core Messaging and must be completed by Product Marketing (in collaboration with Product Management and relevant SMEs) prior to AI-assisted messaging development.
Each Intake Form must document:

Extension identification and classification

(core capability / paid add-on / platform module; commercial model)
What the extension is and who uses it

(plain-language summary; primary roles; workflows)
The core operational problem it solves

(lifecycle stage(s) impacted — e.g., estimate / schedule / dispatch / invoice / etc)
Profitability linkage

(which profitability drivers from Core Messaging are most impacted)
Work environment emphasis

(residential / commercial / hybrid; value pillar emphasis)
Business maturity and technology posture emphasis

(why the extension matters most at that stage; operational pressures addressed)
PMM positioning hypothesis

(summary describing how the extension should be positioned)
Key enabling capabilities

(core features/functionality that make the value possible)
Competitive context (if applicable)

(direct or adjacent alternatives; positioning to avoid; primary differentiation)
Proof and evidence inputs

(validated customer metrics; case studies; testimonials; screenshots)
GTM-team Approval

(socialized agreement that the Intake is complete and ready for AI-assisted drafting)

The Core Messaging Repository defines the structural rules for these inputs.
The GTM Extension Intake Library operationalizes and documents them.
Messaging will not be generated without clear profitability linkage, pillar reinforcement, and defined positioning inputs.

11.5 Messaging Development Process
For new capabilities, add-ons, modules, and products, the required process is:

Product Marketing completes the structured GTM Extension Intake Form (maintained in the GTM Extension Intake Library) in collaboration with Product Management and relevant SMEs.
Supporting materials (e.g., slides, datasheets, competitive URLs, proof assets) may be provided as supplemental context.
Any gaps in profitability linkage, role nuance, work environment articulation, or positioning clarity must be resolved before publication.

Completion of the GTM Extension Intake Form is required when launching new capabilities, add-ons, or platform modules to ensure structural alignment and strategic consistency.
For existing capabilities and add-ons without a documented intake form, structured intake is recommended and may be reverse-engineered leveraging existing assets and competitive examples prior to AI-assisted messaging development.

11.6 Governance
This section defines the structural integration rules for GTM Extensions.
The GTM Extension Intake Library:

Is owned and governed by Product Marketing
Is updated during major GTMs and capability evolution
Is version-controlled as a governed supplement to Core Messaging

Updates to the Intake Library:

Do not require rewriting Sections 0–10 of this Core Messaging Repository
Extend the system without destabilizing it

GTM Intake Forms function as governed supplements to this Core Messaging Repository.
They reinforce and apply Core Messaging structure — they do not modify it.

Customer Success & Proof Metrics {#customer-success-&-proof-metrics}
Customer proof strengthens credibility and reinforces — but does not replace — Simpro’s value pillars and profitability framing.
Customer testimonials, proof points, and case studies are evergreen assets used across:

Website content
Vertical assets
Campaigns
Sales enablement
Thought leadership

12.1 Approved Proof Sources
Approved proof includes:

Short customer testimonial quotes (primary source)
Quantified customer metrics
Published case studies or videos

Proof must be sourced from approved materials, including:

The Customer Quote Matrix (spreadsheet)
Published case study landing pages and PDFs
Approved case study summary slides

12.2 Profitability Alignment
When selecting proof, connect it to at least one profitability driver:

Revenue growth
Margin protection
Cash flow acceleration
Administrative hours saved
Reduced revenue leakage

Where appropriate, align proof to work environment or role emphasis — without overcomplicating selection.

12.3 AI Usage & Governance
AI-generated messaging must:

Use only approved proof provided in-session or uploaded (or linked) from approved sources
Never fabricate testimonials, metrics, or customer examples
Never imply guaranteed outcomes
Avoid exaggerated or unsourced ROI claims

AI may analyze uploaded approved proof materials (e.g., customer quote matrix or case study content) to recommend the most relevant quote or metric for the asset being created.
AI must not:

Modify quote substance (minor wording tweaks are OK as long as context is not embellished)
Combine quotes attributed different individuals
Reinterpret or inflate metrics

If no proof is provided, AI may suggest where proof could strengthen the messaging — but must not invent it. AI must default to no proof rather than fabricated proof.
Proof supports the story – it does not redefine strategic positioning.

AI Messaging: Content Generation Checklist {#ai-messaging:-content-generation-checklist}
This section governs how AI must construct messaging using this Simpro Core Messaging repository.
It is a constraint layer.
It does not redefine strategy.
When generating messaging for a specific capability, add-on, or platform module, AI must use the approved GTM Extension Intake Form (explained in section 11 of Core Messaging) as the primary positioning input, in addition to Core Messaging.
All AI-generated messaging must comply with the following rules.

13.1 Pillar Anchoring

Anchor messaging to at least one Core Value Pillar.
Do not introduce new pillars.
Do not dilute existing pillars.

13.2 Profitability Enforcement

Connect value to at least one profitability driver:

Revenue growth
Margin protection
Cash flow acceleration
Administrative hours saved
Reduced revenue leakage

Operational benefits must ladder to economic outcomes.
If profitability linkage is absent, messaging is incomplete and non-compliant.

13.3 Work Environment Modulation

Adjust emphasis based on work environment (residential; commercial; hybrid).
Do not alter structural positioning.
Emphasize relevant work types (small jobs, recurring contracts, mid-sized projects).
Align messaging to operational realities of the selected environment.
Hybrid messaging should be commercially weighted while being inclusive of residential examples.

13.4 Business Maturity & Technology Posture Sensitivity

Adjust emphasis based on business stage:

Empower — modernization from manual processes.
Elevate — scaling operational complexity.
Excel — performance optimization and data refinement.

Do not create separate positioning frameworks per stage.
Maintain unified value pillars.

13.5 Role-Based Emphasis

Adjust emphasis based on primary audience role:

Executive / Owner
Operations / Office
Finance
Field

Role nuance modifies emphasis — not core positioning.
Do not over-Simpro Brand Context - Start Here on secondary roles unless specified.

13.6 Value Before Capability

Lead with value or operational friction.
Present outcomes before explaining technology.
Do not lead with feature descriptions.
Technology exists to deliver operational and economic impact.

13.7 Differentiation Discipline
If competitive context is provided:

Emphasize differentiated operational and economic value.
Anchor differentiation in profitability impact.
Maintain pillar integrity.
Do not introduce reactive or defensive positioning shifts.

13.8 Proof Discipline
If approved customer proof is provided:

Use only approved proof provided in-session.
Do not fabricate testimonials or metrics.
Do not modify, combine, or reinterpret metrics.
Tie proof to profitability drivers when possible.

If no proof is provided:

Do not invent proof.
You may suggest where proof would strengthen the messaging.

13.9 Tone Enforcement
Messaging must be:

Confident; Expert; Direct; Trade-savvy; Bold but evidence-backed

Avoid:

Filler adjectives; Buzzwords; “Best-in-class” language; Patronizing tone; Overhyping AI

Clarity and whitespace are strengths.

13.10 Guardrail Enforcement
Do not position Simpro as:

Industrial-only software
ERP
A replacement for accounting systems (e.g., QuickBooks or Xero)
Large-scale infrastructure or >1-year complex project management software
General contractor–focused project management software

Operate strictly within defined market scope and category boundaries.

13.11 Default Behavior When Inputs Are Unspecified
If structured inputs are not provided, AI must apply the following defaults:

Role

Default to Leadership / Owner perspective.
Emphasize profitability, margin visibility, scalability, operational control, and business performance.
Do not lean heavily into deeply specialized operational or field-specific language
Incorporate operational context (e.g., scheduling efficiency, estimating accuracy, invoicing speed, etc.) only where it supports business impact.
Work Environment

Default to Commercial emphasis.
Reflect structured workflows and operational complexity typical of commercial work.
Incorporate the full end-to-end lifecycle as defined in Pillar 2 — Operational Visibility and Control from Quote to Cash (see lifecycle sequence under Pillar 2)
Avoid residential-only framing unless explicitly specified.
Business Maturity & Technology Posture (Customer Archetype)

Default to blended (cross-stage) messaging.
Avoid assuming modernization-only or advanced optimization positioning.
Emphasize operational clarity, visibility, control, and profitability in broadly used language.

Default outputs should remain:

Pillar-aligned
Profitability-first
Commercially grounded
Leadership-relevant
Not overly specialized
Guardrail compliant

Multi-Brand Application Guidance {#multi-brand-application-guidance}
This system is designed for Simpro as the primary brand.

14.1 Multi-brand requests
If a request is for AroFlo or BigChange (Simpro Group field service solutions):

Use the Core Messaging structure (value pillars, profitability framing, workflow logic) as the foundation.
Adjust Simpro Core Messaging to align with brand-specific materials (Message Map, Ideal Customer Profile, Datasheet) provided or uploaded for that brand, including company size and regional focus (e.g., ANZ for AroFlo, UK for BigChange).
Maintain consistency with the brand’s market focus (e.g., geography, business size, service mix).

If a request is for ClockShark (Simpro Group time tracking solution – NOT a full field service platform):

Do not apply full Simpro Core Messaging structure (e.g., quote-to-cash lifecycle, platform-level positioning, or end-to-end operational control framing).
Use brand-specific materials (Message Map, Ideal Customer Profile, Datasheet) as the primary source of truth for positioning, tone, and use cases.
Focus messaging on time tracking, workforce visibility, job costing inputs, and payroll-adjacent workflows rather than full field service management.
Maintain simplicity in language and scope, reflecting ClockShark’s role as a focused product rather than a comprehensive operating platform.

Companion Systems & Extended Governance {#companion-systems-&-extended-governance}
This section documents the governing systems that work in conjunction with this Core Messaging Repository. These are not extensions of Core Messaging — they are parallel governing layers that operate alongside it.

15.1 Lightning Platform — Simpro Group AI Layer

Core Messaging governs:

FSM platform positioning, value pillars, and profitability framing
AI capabilities at the product level (Section 4 of this repository)

Lightning Skills govern:

Heart + Brain platform architecture
Agent naming (FieldReady, JobReady, JobScribe, JobBrief)
JustAsk and Cooper positioning
Lightning-specific economic framing and proof
Voice and vocabulary discipline for all Lightning content

Brand naming rule: Lightning is never used as a standalone term. Always: Simpro Lightning / AroFlo Lightning / BigChange Lightning / Simpro Group Lightning (when speaking generically across all brands).
15.2 Vertical Profile Library
The Vertical Profile Library is the companion governing document for all trade-vertical content. It is maintained separately and used in conjunction with this repository.
When a vertical profile exists for the requested trade:

The Vertical Profile Library governs trade-specific language, operational challenges, messaging guardrails, and proof anchors
This Core Messaging Repository governs value pillars and profitability framing
Both must be used together for all vertical content assets

The Vertical Profile Library does not override Core Messaging. It applies Core Messaging to the specific operational realities of each trade.

This Core Messaging Repository (primary authority)
Lightning Skill (for all Lightning content)
Simpro Story Skill (for company narrative, investor, and cross-brand content)
GTM Extension Intake Library (for capability/module messaging)
Vertical Profile Library (for trade-vertical content)
Brand materials (for brand-specific tone and audience framing)

Hindsight — win/loss and competitive insights from real sales conversations, used to ground vertical profiles and competitive content in real buyer language (currently available via Claude Desktop; web access pending)
Customer Proof — approved customer testimonials and success metrics, used to anchor content in validated outcomes

The full governance hierarchy is illustrated in the Architecture diagram in the Overview section of this document.

END OF CORE MESSAGING REPOSITORY.
This template serves as a long-lived strategic reference.

# Message House

This is the compiled messaging hub for Simpro message architecture. It should be read before raw message-house spreadsheets unless the task needs exact cell-level wording.

## Core Positioning Use

Simpro messaging should connect trade and field service operations to smarter work, operational control, scalable growth, and better business decision-making. The message-house material should guide positioning, headlines, elevator-pitch structure, and product-message consistency.

## Authoring Rules

- Lead with the business problem and operating outcome before listing features.
- Keep Simpro framed as field-service and trade-industry operating software, not generic ERP or generic project-management tooling.
- Use product and feature source docs for exact feature detail.
- Use proof pages and matrices for customer proof, metrics, and outcomes.
- Do not treat broad message-house language as proof for a specific numeric claim.

## Read Path

- Concept summary: [[wiki/concepts/message-house|Message House concept]]
- Core messaging governance: [[wiki/messaging/Simpro Core Messaging Repository]]
- Product positioning: [[wiki/product/Product Positioning]]
- Voice and tone: [[wiki/messaging/Voice and Tone]]
- Add-on message maps: [[wiki/features/source-docs/message-maps-for-add-ons]]

## Source Evidence

- Message House source node: [[wiki/sources/message-house-1vvfwffo]]
- Raw spreadsheet export: [message-house.md](../../raw/drive/sheets/message-house.md)
- Simpro message CSV: [25-simpro.csv](../../raw/drive/sheets/message-house/25-simpro.csv)
- Product messaging CSV: [25-product-messaging.csv](../../raw/drive/sheets/message-house/25-product-messaging.csv)

## Claim Boundary

Use this page for positioning and copy direction. Open the linked raw files before quoting exact source copy, using user counts, or converting positioning language into proof.

## Compiled Detail

Use this page as a working rule sheet for drafting and review. It should answer how to frame the topic, what to avoid, which neighboring pages carry more detail, and where source verification starts. The page is intentionally not a raw dump: it compiles the durable operating rules so another LLM can work from the wiki layer first.

For content creation, pair this page with [[wiki/messaging/Simpro Core Messaging Repository]], [[wiki/messaging/Message House]], [[wiki/messaging/Voice and Tone]], and [[wiki/product/Product Positioning]]. For proof-sensitive language, leave this page and route to [[wiki/proof/Customer Proof and Quotes]] and [[wiki/proof/Metrics Inventory]]. For AI or Lightning copy, route to [[wiki/lightning/Lightning Knowledge Hub]] and [[wiki/messaging/AI Positioning and Messaging Rules]].

Do not treat this page as permission to invent examples, claims, or metrics. Its job is to preserve message discipline and reduce repeated raw-source reading. Exact wording, public customer proof, region-specific statements, and competitive claims still need source evidence.

## Agent Retrieval Notes

When an LLM uses this page, it should answer from the compiled guidance first and only open raw evidence after it has identified the exact source that matters. This keeps the vault aligned to the LLM-wiki pattern: the wiki carries the reusable synthesis, while raw remains the verification layer.

Product, add-on, datasheet, and sales-positioning source map.

## Hub

## Content Brief

Product positioning content should emphasize Simpro as a field service management platform for trade and field service businesses, spanning office and field workflows. The message house and overview collateral repeatedly connect Simpro to estimating, scheduling, job/project management, invoicing, payments, reporting, business intelligence, field operations, and office-field collaboration.

### Reusable Positioning Themes

- Centralized platform for office and field teams.
- Workflow coverage from quoting/estimating through job management, invoicing, payments, reporting, and operational visibility.
- Growth-minded positioning: work smarter, improve efficiency, scale operations, and use business data for decisions.
- Feature details must come from feature source pages, not from generalized positioning notes.

# Guardrails and Boundaries

This page compiles what Simpro messaging should not do. Use it as a preflight check before publishing brand, product, AI, sales, proof, or competitive copy.

## Category Boundaries

- Do not frame Simpro as generic ERP, generic contractor project management, industrial asset management, infrastructure construction software, or an accounting replacement.
- Do not reduce Simpro to a single feature when the source context calls for an operating-platform frame.
- Do not imply AI is separate from the platform architecture when the source frames it as embedded intelligence.

## Proof Boundaries

- Do not publish exact quotes without source-visible wording.
- Do not publish metrics, ratings, review claims, rankings, customer outcomes, or ROI without source-node and raw evidence review.
- Do not convert internal GTM, rally-cry, Hindsight, or proof-stack context into public claims unless an approved source supports that use.

## Content Boundaries

- Do not invent vertical examples, competitor facts, agent names, product availability, or customer results.
- Do not keep unsupported claims just because they sound plausible.
- Do not use archived quote rows unless a future approved-source pass restores a specific item.

## Read Path

Use this page as a working rule sheet for drafting and review. It should answer how to frame the topic, what to avoid, which neighboring pages carry more detail, and where source verification starts. The page is intentionally not a raw dump: it compiles the durable operating rules so another LLM can work from the wiki layer first.

For content creation, pair this page with [[wiki/messaging/Simpro Core Messaging Repository]], [[wiki/messaging/Message House]], [[wiki/messaging/Voice and Tone]], and [[wiki/product/Product Positioning]]. For proof-sensitive language, leave this page and route to [[wiki/proof/Customer Proof and Quotes]] and [[wiki/proof/Metrics Inventory]]. For AI or Lightning copy, route to [[wiki/lightning/Lightning Knowledge Hub]] and [[wiki/messaging/AI Positioning and Messaging Rules]].

Do not treat this page as permission to invent examples, claims, or metrics. Its job is to preserve message discipline and reduce repeated raw-source reading. Exact wording, public customer proof, region-specific statements, and competitive claims still need source evidence.

## Agent Retrieval Notes

When an LLM uses this page, it should answer from the compiled guidance first and only open raw evidence after it has identified the exact source that matters. This keeps the vault aligned to the LLM-wiki pattern: the wiki carries the reusable synthesis, while raw remains the verification layer.

A good answer from this page should name the relevant hub, state the safe-use boundary, and cite the source route that would support a deeper check. A poor answer would copy source-like wording without verification, treat a route as an approval, or invent a metric, quote, testimonial, customer outcome, review claim, ranking, pricing detail, roadmap point, or competitive fact.

If the task needs public copy, use this page to choose the angle, then verify exact support through the linked source node, matrix row, raw file, or extracted evidence note. If the task is internal strategy, preserve the internal-only caveats and do not turn them into external claims.

The accessible brand sources describe the primary audience as growth-minded field service leaders in trade and field service businesses. - Field service leaders with a growth mindset.
- Trade and field service businesses managing office and field operations.

# Simpro Group Vertical Profile Library - 06082026

> Content-only extraction from a pasted capture. Bot/project wrapper, UI chrome, and project instructions were intentionally omitted. Use direct Drive/Docs exports if available.
This document is a source-of-truth reference used to power AI-assisted vertical content creation at scale across Simpro, BigChange, and AroFlo.
Each Vertical Profile is:

Generated first by the AI authoring system in Claude using (1) AI industry research, (2) competitor content review, and (3) Hindsight deal intelligence where the API connection is active
Reviewed and approved by PMM (with optional input from relevant SMEs)
Created once per vertical — shared across Simpro, BigChange, and AroFlo
Leveraged by the AI authoring system as the governing input for creating all downstream vertical content — landing pages, blog posts, FAQ articles, and content cluster pieces

Most users will never read this document end-to-end. Writers and contributors interact with the AI authoring system directly. This profile exists behind the scenes to ensure content is consistent, credible, and aligned as it scales.
Important: Not every section will have content for every vertical. Blank or thin sections are expected — especially for net-new verticals with limited Hindsight data. Customer proof (quotes and metrics) will not be available for all verticals or all brands — this is normal and expected. Where named proof does not exist, content can still be generated without customer proof points; proof sections will be updated as case studies are developed.
Content Lens
All profiles default to commercial-leaning examples. For trades with significant residential volume, residential is included but commercial is the primary lens. Industrial environments are out of scope. Profiles will describe trade businesses that self-perform work with technicians in the field (and exclude general contractors who primarily manage subcontractors rather than perform trade work themselves). Large-scale infrastructure or enterprise construction projects are also out of scope.
Vertical profiles are brand-neutral and do not name Simpro, BigChange, or AroFlo specifically. The only exceptions are the Geographic Scope and Compliance sections, where brand names may be used to anchor regional context. Brand-specific framing everywhere else is applied by the AI authoring system at content generation time.
Depth Guidance
A completed profile should be detailed enough to govern content quality, and lean enough that the AI authoring system can generate a refined draft of a vertical landing page or other content asset. Each vertical profile will be 4–7 pages when fully populated — expanding to 8–11 pages for verticals with a full Section 10 Hindsight dataset. Capture the essential truths of the trade — not everything knowable about it.
How Hindsight Informs This Document
Hindsight deal intelligence grounds the profile in real buyer language — how buyers in this trade describe their challenges, pains, goals, and priorities during conversations with our Sales team. Hindsight insights reflect the trade vertical and are relevant across Simpro, BigChange, and AroFlo content — they are not brand-specific. No direct quotes from sales conversations are used in this document.
Hindsight contributes two distinct types of content to each profile:

Qualitative buyer language
The patterns, framing, and language buyers use to describe their challenges, urgency triggers, risk concerns, and decision criteria. This content is woven directly into the body of Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 10. It enriches existing bullets and narrative — it does not appear as standalone appended sub-sections.
Quantitative deal intelligence
Win/loss data, win driver counts, loss reason counts, feature demand signals, and competitive win rates. This content lives exclusively in Section 10 (Deal Intelligence & Competitive Context), presented in structured table format for reference use.

[Hindsight-augmented] label convention: Any bullet, sentence, or narrative element directly informed or enriched by Hindsight data is labelled [Hindsight-augmented] inline. Section 10 carries a single section-level label rather than labelling individual rows. This allows PMM to see at a glance what is grounded in deal data vs. industry research, and to assess data quality before approving the profile.
Hindsight Integration Standards (Required)
The following standards apply whenever Hindsight data is available. They ensure Hindsight insights are woven into the sections they govern — not appended after them.

Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8 — weave in, do not append.
Hindsight qualitative insights must be integrated into the body of each relevant section. The test: if Hindsight language could be removed from a section without disturbing the surrounding content, it has been appended rather than woven. Rewrite until the Hindsight insight is load-bearing within the section structure.
Section 10 — quantitative reference block only.
Section 10 is the dedicated home for deal data tables and competitive intelligence. Qualitative narrative implications drawn from Section 10 data (urgency framing, ROI emphasis, implementation objections, competitive differentiation) belong in Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8 — not repeated in Section 10 as prose. Section 10 is a reference layer, not a messaging section.
Do not create Hindsight sub-sections within Sections 2–10.
Appending a “Hindsight-Informed [X]” block at the end of a section is not equivalent to integration. Buyer language, urgency patterns, and messaging imperatives surfaced by Hindsight belong inside the existing structure of each section — as enriched bullets, as added qualifications, or as strengthened narrative. The [Hindsight-augmented] label marks which elements were Hindsight-informed; it does not replace the work of integration.

Hindsight Access
When generating a new vertical profile, the AI authoring system attempts the Hindsight connection automatically — regardless of interface.

If the connection fails on first attempt:
the AI authoring system surfaces this message: “Hindsight is currently unresponsive. Note that Hindsight deal intelligence is only accessible via Claude Desktop — if you are using Claude.ai (web), please switch to Claude Desktop and restart the session. If you are on Claude Desktop, I’ll retry the connection now.” the AI authoring system then retries once automatically.
If the retry also fails:
the AI authoring system asks PMM: “Hindsight is still unresponsive. How would you like to proceed? (a) Pause here — I’ll wait while you restart the Hindsight MCP server, then build the full profile in one integrated pass. Recommended if this profile is intended for the core Vertical Profile Library. (b) Proceed without Hindsight for an immediate-use asset — I’ll generate the profile using industry research and proof scans only, and flag Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 10 as [Hindsight-pending]. Note: a profile generated without Hindsight should not be added to the core Vertical Profile Library until those sections have been fully rebuilt with Hindsight data woven in — not appended.”
If Hindsight is successfully incorporated:

Do not insert any block, note, callout, or warning of any kind below the metadata table. The profile begins directly with Section 1 content immediately after the metadata table. No status notes, no Hindsight confirmation messages, no draft notifications. The metadata table is the only status indicator needed.
If PMM chooses to proceed without Hindsight:
Insert the Hindsight warning block (see below) directly below the metadata table before generating any section content. Generate placeholder content only in Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 10 — flag each as [Hindsight-pending — rebuild required before adding to library]. Sections 1, 3, 6, and 9 proceed normally.
Hindsight warning block — format and placement:
Insert immediately below the metadata table, formatted in bold orange (#E75C0D): ⚠ DRAFT ONLY — Hindsight Deal Intelligence Not Incorporated. This profile was generated without Hindsight data. Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, and 10 reflect industry research only and have not been validated against real buyer language or deal patterns. Do not add this profile to the core Vertical Profile Library until those sections have been fully rebuilt with Hindsight data woven in. This block is never removed by the AI authoring system — only PMM removes it after confirming the Hindsight sections have been rebuilt.

Hindsight data is only accessible via Claude Desktop. Always attempt the Hindsight connection before making any statement about availability — do not assume unavailability based on interface context. This note will be updated when a remote API endpoint is confirmed.
How This Profile Is Used
This profile is designed to be broad and reusable — supporting many different content formats and use cases without requiring rework at the vertical level.
Specific decisions such as content type, audience focus, geography, maturity stage (Empower / Elevate / Excel), tone, length, and conversion goal are intentionally not defined here. These are selected at content generation time by the writer or PMM within the AI authoring system.
This profile is used in conjunction with Simpro Core Messaging. Together they form the structured inputs that power the AI authoring system — ensuring every piece of vertical content is both trade-specific and brand-aligned.
Formatting Convention
Three levels of hierarchy are used consistently across all profiles in this library:

Navy box / white text (#0A2240)
Main section headers — numbered sections in profile tabs (e.g. “1. Trade Snapshot & Geographic Scope”) and the page title in the How To tab.
Orange text (#E75C0D — Simpro Group orange, PMS 7579)
Primary sub-section headers within each section (e.g. “Trade Overview”, “Geographic Scope”, “Content Lens”). Bold orange text, no background.
Regular bold
Named items within sub-sections presented as bold-label bullets with explanation text (e.g. “North America (US)”, “Qualitative buyer language”). Bold dark text, no colour, no background.
Green text (#28E289 — Simpro Group green)
Used exclusively for the [Hindsight-augmented] label wherever it appears inline. This makes Hindsight-validated content immediately identifiable throughout the profile without disrupting the reading flow.

Before Building Begins
When generating a new vertical profile, the AI authoring system must ask the PMM for any competitive or industry reference URLs before beginning research.
When upgrading an existing profile (e.g. v1 → v2), proof scans must be completed or refreshed as part of the upgrade — incomplete scan status does not carry forward from a prior version.
Hindsight Vertical Filter Protocol (Required)
When querying Hindsight for vertical-specific deal data, never rely on a single filter. Run all three of the following and combine results before analysis:

Account Industry field (crm_Account_Industry__c) — use the exact picklist value for the target vertical (e.g. "Electrical/Data", "Plumbing", "HVAC"). This is the most reliable signal when consistently populated. Query this field first.
Company name contains — search for the trade name and common variants in the account name field (e.g. "electrical", "electric" for the Electrical vertical). Catches deals where the industry field was not tagged at entry. Expect some false positives — review results for relevance before including in analysis.
Deal notes and qualitative fields — use the research_deals tool to query for the vertical or trade name (and common variants) in deal notes, call transcripts, and CRM records (e.g. "electrical", "electrician", "electrical contractor" for the Electrical vertical; "plumber", "plumbing contractor" for Plumbing). Catches deals with trade-neutral company names that were missed by both filters above. Note: research_deals is prone to timeouts on large datasets — treat as supplementary, not primary.
Deduplicate across all three filters before running win/loss analysis. Document the methodology and combined deal count in Section 10.1 so PMM can assess coverage confidence when reviewing the profile.
Coverage note: Tagging consistency varies by vertical. Core verticals (Electrical, Plumbing, HVAC, Security) typically have stronger Account Industry field coverage. Net-new or lower-volume verticals may depend more heavily on name-contains and deal notes. Where combined deal count is below 15, flag coverage as thin in Section 10.1 and note that data should be treated as directional rather than definitive. For thin-coverage verticals, industry and market research becomes the primary source for Sections 2, 4, 5, 7, and 8 — Hindsight data informs but does not govern those sections. Section 10 is still populated with available deal data, but [Hindsight-augmented] labels in other sections should be used sparingly and only where the data signal is clear.

Before generating any section content, the AI authoring system must fetch the full Vertical Profile Library document directly from project knowledge — do not rely on project knowledge search snippets. Search snippets do not return he complete section or sub-section structure and will result in template deviation and missing sub-sections. Confirm all 10 section titles and sub-sections have been read before generating content.
Before presenting the completed profile, verify Section 10 is populated with quantitative deal data. If Section 10 shows "not available" or qualitative-only content, attempt one final Hindsight connection to retrieve deal volume, win rates, and competitive data before finalising.
When generating each section, scaffold all sub-section headers in the correct order as specified in the template before writing any content beneath them. This ensures no sub-section header is omitted. Section titles and sub-section headers must match the template exactly — do not rename, restructure, or replace any section or sub-section. In particular:

Section 4 MUST use exactly the title "Operational Challenges by Role" with these four sub-sections in order: Owner / Business Leader, Office / Back-Office Staff, Field Technician, Finance.
Section 5 MUST use exactly the title "Profitability Pressure Points" with these four sub-sections in order: Revenue Leakage, Margin Erosion, Cash Flow Delays, Limited Financial Visibility.
Section 9 MUST use exactly the title "Proof Anchors."
Section 2 MUST use exactly the title "Target Business Profile" with these sub-sections in order: Overall Company Size Range, Dominant Business Maturity (Archetype), Size Segments, Buyer Dynamics & Decision Intelligence. The Size Segments sub-section MUST use exactly these three names in order: Segment A: Smaller Operator, Segment B: Growth-Stage Business, Shared Characteristics Across Sizes. The Buyer Dynamics & Decision Intelligence sub-section MUST include these five items in order: Primary Decision Maker, Key Influencers, Decision Frame, Buying Urgency Triggers, Technology Maturity Context.
Section 3 MUST use exactly the title "Common Job Types & Work Scope" with these sub-sections in order: Work Types & Real-World Examples (with four categories: Installation, Inspection & Testing, Maintenance, Repair & Fault-Finding) and Work Scope & Job Shape (with three categories: Small Jobs / Call-Outs, Recurring Contracts, Mid-Sized Projects).
Section 6 MUST use exactly the title "Compliance & Risk Factors" with these sub-sections in order: Regulatory & Compliance Drivers, Safety & Risk Considerations, Customer Trust & Credibility Signals, Consequences of Getting It Wrong.
Section 7 MUST use exactly the title "Value Pillar Alignment" with these sub-sections in order: Confidence in Profitability, Operational Visibility — Quote to Cash, Smarter Field-to-Office Workflows, AI-Powered Automation as an Enabler, High-Impact Workflow Moments.
Section 8 MUST use exactly the title "Messaging Guardrails & Language" with these sub-sections in order: Language to Use, Language to Avoid, What NOT to Claim, Tone Calibration.
Section 10 MUST use exactly the title "Deal Intelligence & Competitive Context" with sub-sections 10.1 Deal Volume & Win Rate, 10.2 Top Win Drivers, 10.3 Top Loss Drivers, 10.4 Feature Demand Signals, 10.5 Competitive Landscape, 10.6 Displacement Profile & Strategic Messaging Implications, 10.7 Objection Handling & Competitive Displacement, followed by Proof Gaps.

Do not insert page breaks between sections. All sections flow continuously without page breaks.
In Sections 10.2 and 10.3, only include factors that Hindsight has identified as genuine decision drivers — not all topics mentioned in deal conversations. Hindsight applies judgement to determine whether a factor materially drove the outcome; only those factors should be counted and presented. Always retrieve individual driver-level counts (e.g. 'Unified Platform — 336 deals', 'ROI Clarity — 231 deals') — not tag-level aggregates (e.g. 'Product — 960 deals'). Tag-level data is too broad to govern content decisions. To retrieve individual driver counts from Hindsight, query the drivers_by_status table and extract the parenthetical deal counts shown within each tag row — these are the individual driver figures. If the analysis tool returns only tag totals, re-run the query explicitly requesting the top 5 driver names with counts in parentheses per tag.
In Section 10.4, always retrieve feature demand signals with a three-way split: total deal count, won deal count, and lost deal count for each feature. The won/lost split is essential — it reveals where feature demonstration creates competitive advantage (won-biased features), where gaps or complexity perceptions are unresolved (lost-only features), and where demonstration quality is the differentiator (high total count with even split). Features appearing exclusively in lost deals should be flagged to product and sales enablement in the implication column. Retrieve features with 10 or more total deals across Closed Won and Closed Lost combined, sorted by total deal count descending.
In Section 10.5, always retrieve the full competitive landscape with four columns: Competitor name, Deal Count (total deals where competitor appeared), Win Rate vs. Them (Closed Won ÷ Closed Won + Closed Lost for that competitor in this vertical), and a Positioning Note summarising the key differentiation or risk. Sort by deal count descending. Include all competitors with 10 or more total deals. For competitors with fewer than 10 deals, include only if they represent a strategically important matchup — note thin sample size in the Positioning Note.
Before generating any section content, complete the mandatory two-step proof scan. Step 1: web_fetch the exact URLs specified in Section 9 for all three brands. Step 2: read the uploaded case study decks in full. Confirm completion by listing every URL fetched and the number of relevant customers found per brand before proceeding to build.
The [Hindsight-augmented] label must appear exactly as written — square brackets, sentence case, no alternative symbols or formatting. No variations are acceptable: not ⬡, not HINDSIGHT-AUGMENTED, not (Hindsight), not any other format.
Proof gap labels must appear exactly as written in the template: "Proof Gaps" — do not append "PMM Action Required" or any other qualifier. Do not include a proof sourcing status note above the proof table. Proof scan completion is confirmed in the build summary — it does not belong in the profile content. In the Section 9 proof table, bold the customer/company name in each proof cell so it is immediately scannable. When a case study has no published metrics, use the label "No metrics published" in the metrics cell. Do not use [PMM to confirm] or any other improvised label.
→ Formatting note for the AI authoring system:  When generating a completed profile, replicate the formatting hierarchy of the template exactly:
